problems.problem: `capy kick --web` has no working "no". I drove the real confirm-remove page: its buttons are ["Remove member","Keep them","copy"], and clicking "Keep them" — the answer the terminal DEFAULTS to — submits nothing. 1.5s after the click the promise is still PENDING; it ends `REJECTED: Timed out waiting for the browser`. In production kickCommand passes no timeoutMs, so that is the runBrowserWizard default of FIVE MINUTES before the CLI prints "Cancelled." Meanwhile the view flips client-side to the roster and tells an owner "Your role — owner — can see the roster but cannot change roles or grants", which is false (a consequence of `assignableRoles: []`). Both are disclosed in the report as packages/ui limitations and the outcome fails safe (nobody is removed), but the flow shipped with no in-repo mitigation (e.g. a short timeoutMs for kick, or refusing --web for kick until the screen posts a cancel) and — tellingly — the only "no" browser test written is `closing the window removes nobody`, never a click on the actual No control. The one path a click would have exposed is the one path that was not clicked.

Zero command-level tests. There is no tests/commands/inviteCommand.test.ts and nothing anywhere imports InviteCommand (tests/commands/inviteFlow.test.ts is pure crypto). ~200 new lines of --web branching — settledRole, settledExpiry, envTtl, resolveProjectTokens, gatherWebParams, the browser branch gate `webParams && unansweredInviteStops(plan).length > 0`, finalStops, and the serveInviteCode call site — are exercised by nothing. Most importantly the load-bearing security claim of the whole commit, "THE REDEEM CODE STOPS BEING PRINTED" under --web, has no test at all. Code reading confirms it holds today (the `console.log(... redeem ${redeemCode})` at line 541 sits in the non-web else branch, and the clipboard prompt is gated on `interactive && !webParams`), but the invariant is unpinned and one refactor from silently regressing. kickCommand.test.ts got exactly this treatment (+86 lines, including the CAPY_WEB_NO_OPEN assertion); inviteCommand got none.

--web changes logic, not only rendering, in two ways the brief's rule ("--web changes the RENDERING of a question, never the logic") forbids on its face. (1) `canAskExpiry: opts.web === true` adds a FOURTH question the terminal never asks, so `capy invite bob` and `capy invite bob --web` can mint invites with different lifetimes from identical argv. (2) --web suppresses the redeem code from stdout entirely and hands back a URL instead. Both are deliberate, argued at length in the file header and commit message, and contract.ts explicitly sanctions the expiry stop ("A CLI implementing this contract may serve it or skip it"). Flagging for the coordinator as a scope/consistency call rather than a bug — but it is a divergence the partition doc does not authorise on its own.

The finished rail lies on a --web re-issue. `capy invite <existing-member> --web` with no --role takes the "pure re-issue" branch, so no browser ever opens and the invite is minted with the default TTL — but `canAskExpiry` is still true when finalStops is built, so the rail reports expiry as outstanding on a completed run. I reproduced it directly: `step = code` while `stops = [["role","done"],["projects","done"],["expiry","current"],["code","upcoming"]]`, identical in the code page's payload and in `capy invite --web --json`'s `stops`. That is precisely the failure invitePlan.ts's own header says the markers exist to prevent — a stop whose state does not describe what the run did. The code view happens not to draw the rail, so the visible damage is confined to --web --json. One-line fix: build finalStops with canAskExpiry false (nothing is outstanding by then), or pass `expiry: {value: <the ttl actually used>, flag: 'default'}`.

`WebInviteParams.rawEmail` is declared (line 107), consumed (line 263 → `rawInviteeEmail`), and unit-tested ('an address argv changed is shown beside the one argv typed'), but `InviteCommand.gatherWebParams` never sets it — grep finds no producer outside the test. So `inviteeEmail` carries argv verbatim while contract.ts documents that field as "trimmed and lowercased", with `rawInviteeEmail` existing specifically to surface the hazard it names: "the CLI lowercases but does not trim, and the untrimmed address is baked into the HKDF salt — so ` bob@x.com` mints a code nobody can ever redeem." A dead affordance and an unmet contract obligation: the one thing the field was added for stays invisible.

The flake is reduced, not eliminated, and the report overstates it as fixed. Across 33 consecutive runs of this file on my machine I saw 1 failure (~3%); the remaining 32 were clean, including two blocks of 12 back to back. I could not re-capture which test lost it. The navigate()/untilSettled() work is real and clearly better than the claimed pre-fix 1-in-3, but 'Verified with 4 consecutive clean e2e runs' is not evidence of determinism at this rate.

Shared-harness edits beyond appending. Besides the mandated +351 lines of new describe blocks, this branch rewrote the `open()` helper inside the three PRE-EXISTING describe blocks (base flow, sync conflict, capy checkout) to route through the new navigate(), and changed a body in the base flow test (`window.answer()` → `void window.answer()`, `until` → `untilSettled`). This is the one file every parcel appends to, so every other in-flight web/* branch will now conflict on those hunks rather than merging cleanly at the tail. The change itself is correct; the placement is a coordination cost the partition doc's per-file ownership rule was written to avoid.

--web is not reachable from argv for either command. index.ts registers `invite` and `kick` without threading the root program's global --web (contrast byoc at line 418 and the `merged.web` path at line 690), so every line of this parcel's browser work is dead code from a real `capy` invocation. The report discloses this and it matches P7/checkout's precedent, and index.ts is in no parcel — but it means nothing here has been exercised through the actual CLI entry point, only through direct calls to memberScreens.ts from tests.
